spans.text: eWAVE variety ID: 15 Variety type: High-contact L1 varieties (L1c) As the label suggests, the varieties in this group are characterized by a high degree of contact between different dialects of English and/or between English and other languages.

entries.description: on that have been formed by settlers with diverse linguistic and/or dialectal backgrounds roughly within the last 400 years
entries.subject: on that
entries.object: been formed by settlers with diverse linguistic and/or dialectal backgrounds roughly within the last 400 years

spans.text: The following three types of varieties are considered high-contact L1 varieties in eWAVE: (a) Transplanted L1 Englishes or colonial (standard) varieties: new indigenized varieties of English with native speakers from early on that have been formed by settlers with diverse linguistic and/or dialectal backgrounds roughly within the last 400 years.

spans.text: (b) Language-shift Englishes: varieties that have replaced the erstwhile primary language in the community and that have adult and child L1 and L2 speakers forming one speech community.

entries.task_id: vernacular english|are|spoken by more than 30 million working-class african americans throughout north america
entries.description: Vernacular English are spoken by more than 30 million working-class African Americans throughout North America
entries.subject: Vernacular English
entries.object: spoken by more than 30 million working-class African Americans throughout North America

spans.text: DESCRIPTION (from the eWAVE chapter on this variety) ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Urban varieties of African American Vernacular English (AAVE) are spoken by more than 30 million working-class African Americans throughout North America, with heavy concentrations of speakers in metropolitan areas such as New York, Philadelphia, Washington, DC, Chicago, Detroit, Houston, and Los Angeles.

entries.task_id: of aave|were|developed or intensified during the twentieth century
entries.description: of AAVE were developed or intensified during the twentieth century
entries.subject: of AAVE
entries.object: developed or intensified during the twentieth century

spans.text: In these segregated urban contexts, many of the contemporary features of AAVE were developed or intensified during the twentieth century, setting these varieties further apart from cohort, working-class white metropolitan communities.

entries.description: AAVE is less likely to show accommodation to regional dialects than in the South
entries.subject: AAVE
entries.object: less likely to show accommodation to regional dialects than in the South

spans.text: In Northern urban areas, AAVE is less likely to show accommodation to regional dialects than in the South.

In more recent decades, a trend of Southern back-migration has taken place, in which cities of the Southern United States such as Atlanta, Charlotte, and Memphis have become prominent contemporary sites for the use of urban AAVE.
